penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Bridging Salesforce field logic to Adobe Sign text tags requires scoping each client's specific Salesforce org configuration, record types, and document templates — Claude can assist but cannot autonomously deliver a working integration without per-customer human configuration work.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise Salesforce admins encountering integration failures will escalate support issues requiring human investigation of their specific org setup.

rationale: The buyer is a specific, named professional (Salesforce admin at a mid-market company) working in a paid enterprise stack worth thousands per year, confirming commercial context and budget authority. However, the actual deliverable — making Salesforce field transformations work inside Adobe Sign text tags — is inherently per-customer and org-specific; there is no universal template that works across all Salesforce configurations. Operational autonomy is therefore structurally low, and the penalty stack drops the total below the validate threshold. A documentation or tutorial product could avoid the fulfillment problem, but buyers in this space expect working solutions, not guides.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable as a scalable autonomous service. Each Salesforce org has unique record types, field names, and document templates — Claude cannot deliver a working Adobe Sign integration without per-customer configuration that requires human involvement. A tutorial library or 'Adobe Sign text tag cookbook' for common Salesforce use cases is buildable autonomously (Claude writes guides, a landing page sells access via Stripe at $49–$99 one-time), but it's unclear whether admins would pay for guides when free Stack Exchange answers already exist. Only pursue if reframed as a pure content/template product — and validate payment intent with a landing page before building.
notes: Failing build_gate: operational_autonomy (5 < 7 required). The per-customer configuration requirement is structural unless the product is reframed as documentation rather than a working integration.
